correctness.rationale: All exact-two histories reduce to P, A or B canonical expansions. The source-indexed two-marker alignment proves that only complementary-neighbor A swaps and complement-run P/A attachments identify expansions. Their rewrite graph is a forest, making the deficit exactly the weighted number of complement-following run letters. A unique constant-run factorization proves the rational enumerator for all even alphabet sizes and lengths. A standard-library checker independently exhausts 35,268 word instances, verifies collision classes and polynomial coefficients. The proof, not the finite experiment, establishes the universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: Two-copy reconstruction ambiguity in a DNA-motivated insertion channel is an intrinsic finite-length object. The result is an exact, linear-time word-specific spectrum, with a rational enumerator at every length and alphabet size; it distinguishes all 6 sphere-size classes for q=4,n=6 rather than only the known maximum. It provides exact sphere-size heterogeneity relevant to finite-block code packing, though optimal code sizes are not claimed.
